commands.review_summary:
The PR normalizes non-finite Active Memory legacy toggle timestamps to `Date.now()` during doctor migration and adds an overflow regression test.

PR surface: Source +1, Tests +38. Total +39 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible with high confidence: raw JSON `1e999` becomes `Infinity`, current main accepts it in the legacy reader, and plugin-state registration rejects it as non-finite.

target.title: fix(active-memory): normalize legacy toggle timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Active Memory doctor migration accepted any numeric legacy `updatedAt` value. JSON overflow values can parse to `Infinity`, which would be imported into plugin state instead of being normalized.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration now accepts only finite legacy timestamps and falls back to `Date.now()` for malformed values, matching the existing fallback behavior for non-number timestamps.

## User Impact

Doctor migration no longer writes non-finite timestamps into Active Memory session-toggle state. Valid finite timestamps are preserved.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-cache-active-memory-doctor-reviewfix node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.test.ts`
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on `extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.ts` and `extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- Claude autoreview: clean after review fix and rebase to `upstream/main`

## Proof

The regression test writes a raw legacy JSON file with `updatedAt: 1e999`, verifies the migration imports the toggle, and proves the imported timestamp is the fixed `Date.now()` value rather than a non-finite number.
